newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak details unbundling process.
newsitem.headline: Malbak details unbundling process.

text.p: Malbak Ltd, the South African diversified industrial holding company which is to unbundle, on Thursday detailed the process by which shareholders are to get parcels of shares in its subsidiaries.

Acting chief executive Peter Beningfield said for every 100 Malbak shares held, shareholders would receive approximately 11.2 shares in Foodcorp Ltd, 61.2 shares in Kohler Ltd, 13.8 shares in South African Druggists Ltd, 14 Ellerine Ltd shares and 36.2 New Clicks Ltd shares.
In addition their holding contained around 588 rand in cash which represented the value that would be realised from disposing of Malbak's unlisted companies, he said.
Beningfield said the primary reason for Malbak's unbundling was the discount at which its shares traded relative to their underlying net asset value (NAV).
Beningfield said the NAV of a Malbak share last Friday was about 24.60 rand, which was 15 percent above the 21.35 rand shares were trading at on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"We don't believe it is correct for our shareholders to hold an investment which is undervalued by the market," Beningfield said.

Earlier this week Malbak said shares in the underlying subsidiaries would be distributed to shareholders as the indicative prices received from parties interested in buying these companies did not reflect the value they could receive after unbundling.
Beningfield said their value was likely to appreciate after unbundling as shares became more tradable.
In conclusion, Beningfield said: "We believe management in our companies is sound and that they are able to retain and create value for Malbak shareholders in their companies."
